title: PRESENT Truncated-Differential Resistance
summary: The paper derives a 26-round attack, but further characterizing PRESENT’s resistance to truncated-differential cryptanalysis remains open.

formal_statement.body: Further characterize $\mathrm{PRESENT}$'s resistance to truncated-differential attacks by obtaining accurate estimates of relevant differential probabilities as the number of rounds increases and by determining whether such properties yield improved reduced-round attacks. The main technical obstacle is that $\mathrm{PRESENT}$'s S-box strong differentials diffuse faster than its strong linear approximations over more rounds. Earlier work used linear approximations to estimate differential probabilities accurately but found no differentials that essentially improved the known 19-round differential attack.

scope.domain: Truncated-differential cryptanalysis of the PRESENT block cipher and its reduced-round variants.
parameters: Number of rounds: governs differential diffusion, probability estimation, and the targeted reduced-round attacks
scope.unresolved_remainder: Obtain accurate estimates of relevant differential probabilities as the round count increases and determine whether they enable improved reduced-round attacks on PRESENT.

citations.label: Links between Truncated Differential and Multidimensional Linear Properties of Block Ciphers and Underlying Attack Complexities

progress.summary: The source calls PRESENT’s resistance to truncated-differential attacks a longstanding open problem and identifies faster diffusion of strong S-box differentials as the main obstacle. It reports a 26-round attack as progress without claiming a complete characterization.
